title: Derive artifact cardinality from the aspect's plurality

facts.note: Task text mentions naming, shaping or interpreting a named artifact. Not limited to any particular document type or phase.

values: artifact name declared, changed or referenced
artifact shape (single item vs collection/array/directory) declared or read
facts.note: Needs an observer that extracts colon-separated artifact names (with or without category segments) and any associated shape, in new or existing text.

values: aspect plurality disagrees with declared cardinality
facts.note: Optional detection signal only, NOT an activation prerequisite: the rule also applies when interpreting conforming names. Identifying the aspect vs category/variant and its plurality requires judgment unless a parser and plural lexicon exist.

fires: An artifact name is declared whose aspect is plural (e.g. scenario:fragments) and its shape must be set.
An existing artifact name with a singular aspect (e.g. scenario:fragment) is read and its cardinality must be interpreted.
An artifact name has a plural category (e.g. commons:ux:foundations:color) and its cardinality must be determined or interpreted.
A name with no category segment (e.g. scenario:fragment) whose cardinality is in question.
A conforming name and shape are being checked or relied on, even when no mismatch exists.
doesNotFire: Text that neither declares, references nor interprets any artifact name or artifact cardinality.
Choosing the physical file/directory layout itself (covered by the logical-physical mapping convention), once cardinality is already settled.
Spelling of plurals (covered by the pluralization convention).

given: An artifact name of colon-separated segments ending in an aspect, optionally preceded by category segments (categories are not required, e.g. scenario:fragment) and optionally followed by a variant.
when: The artifact's cardinality (one item vs collection) is determined or interpreted, whether for a new name or an existing one.
then: Take cardinality from the ASPECT (the final noun before any variant) alone: plural aspect → collection/array schema or directory of items; singular aspect → single-item schema.
prefer: Identify the aspect first (final noun before the variant), then read its plurality to pick or interpret the shape.
Pluralize the aspect when you mean a collection (scenario:fragments → collection); keep it singular for one item (scenario:fragment → one item).
avoid: Inferring cardinality from a category segment: commons:ux:foundations:color is ONE item even though 'foundations' is plural; commons:ux:foundations:colors is an array of colors.
Letting the variant segment change cardinality.
Declaring an array/directory under a singular aspect, or a single-item schema under a plural aspect.
why: Cardinality (single item vs collection) is decided by the aspect's plurality, so the name alone indicates one item or a collection; categories and variants do not affect cardinality.
evidence: For each artifact name, the reviewer identifies the aspect and confirms plural aspect ↔ collection/array schema or directory of items, singular aspect ↔ single-item schema.
Reviewer confirms category and variant segments were not used to decide cardinality.
verifier_detail: Term 'cardinality': single-item vs collection, decided by the aspect's plurality. Values: singular_aspect = single item schema; plural_aspect = collection/array schema or directory of items; category_position = does NOT affect cardinality; variant_position = does NOT affect cardinality.
Aspect = final noun before the variant. Names need not contain a category segment (e.g. scenario:fragment).

Source examples: scenario:fragments -> plural aspect -> collection; scenario:fragment -> singular aspect -> one item; commons:ux:foundations:color -> 'foundations' is a category, 'color' singular -> one item; commons:ux:foundations:colors -> 'colors' plural -> array of colors.
